transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I came in because... I've been having this issue after my late shifts. I'll stop for some food on the way home, but then I just keep going once I get to my apartment. 

Like, I'll finish a full takeout meal, and then I'm eating chips, sweets... really just whatever is in the apartment. And afterward, I'm honestly shocked by how much I actually ate. It's just becoming a problem.
After you eat this way, do you ever try to compensate by making yourself sick, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

Yeah, I do. Sometimes after I get home and eat too much of that takeout or the snacks, I'll... I go to the bathroom and make myself throw up. I just don't want all that food to sit in me and turn into weight.
How often do you find yourself making yourself sick after eating this way—like several times a week, once a week, or less often?

Well, since my apartment move settled into a routine, it's been happening about once a week. Usually, I'll have at least one of those late-night episodes where I eat way past what I meant to. And then, yeah, I'll make myself throw up, or sometimes I'll try to make up for it by skipping breakfast the next day, or forcing myself to go for a really long run. But it's usually at least once a week.
When you eat that large amount of food late at night, do you feel like you lose control over your eating — like you can't stop eating or control what or how much you're eating?

Yeah, I definitely do. Once I start on those nights, it's almost like I'm watching myself from the outside. I'll be in my head telling myself to just put the food away, but... my hands just keep opening containers. I really can't seem to stop myself until everything is just gone.
Do these episodes of eating a lot and then making yourself sick tend to happen during specific times, like always late at night, and do they usually occur when you're alone?

Yeah, it's pretty much always late at night. Usually after I get home from my shift and things are just... quiet. And, um, yeah, I'm always alone when it happens. I don't think I'd ever let myself get like that if someone else was in the apartment with me. It's really just a thing that happens when I'm by myself.
Have you ever gone through periods where you feel like you're eating uncontrollably and then making yourself sick more frequently—like more than once a week—for a stretch of several weeks or longer?

No, not really. It's pretty consistently just been the once a week. I haven't really had a stretch where it was happening multiple times a week for a month or anything like that. It just kind of sticks to that one night.
Do these episodes and the way you deal with them afterward cause you a lot of distress, or affect things like your work, social life, or relationships?

It definitely bothers me. I mean, I'm still showing up for work and getting my job done, so it hasn't messed that up. But socially... yeah. I've started dodging invitations to grab a bite with my coworkers after our shifts. I just make up excuses. And my mornings are pretty much planned around, you know, undoing what I did the night before. Instead of getting extra sleep or running errands, I'm just dealing with the aftermath. So, yeah, it definitely affects things.
During these episodes, do you find yourself eating much more rapidly than normal, like eating in a short amount of time or in a way that feels rushed or uncontrollable?

Yeah, it definitely feels out of control. Um... once I start on those nights, it's almost like I'm watching myself from the outside. I'll be in my head, telling myself to just stop and put the food away, but my hands just keep opening containers. I just keep going until everything is gone. So, yeah, it happens fast because I just can't seem to stop it once it starts.
Do you usually start these late-night eating episodes because you're actually hungry, or do you sometimes eat even when you're not physically hungry?

Well, I'm usually actually hungry when it starts. I mean, by the time I get home from work, it's pretty late and I probably haven't eaten in hours. So my stomach is definitely empty. I don't really think I start eating if I'm not physically hungry... it's more that I start because I need to eat, and then it just turns into that whole thing where I can't stop.
Besides making yourself vomit, do you ever use laxatives, diuretics, or take any other steps to try to prevent weight gain after these eating episodes?

No, I don't use laxatives or pills or anything like that. But after a bad night of eating, I'll definitely make myself run extra miles on the trail the next morning. Or I'll just skip breakfast entirely before my shift. Even if I'm exhausted, I just feel like I have to do it to, you know, undo what I did the night before.

When you have these late-night eating episodes, do you find yourself eating a much larger amount of food than most people would eat in the same amount of time, even considering that you’re home alone and not sharing with anyone?

Yeah, it's definitely a lot more food than a normal person would eat. I mean, that's actually why I came in. After a late shift, I'll stop and grab a full takeout meal on the way home. But then I finish that and just keep going. I'll eat chips, sweets, basically whatever I can find in the apartment. When it's finally over, I look at all the wrappers and empty containers, and I'm honestly just shocked by how much I actually ate.

Even though you mentioned eating a lot during these episodes, do you sometimes feel like you're eating a large amount even when it's not objectively more than most people would eat in the same situation?

No, I don't really think so. I mean, when I say I'm eating a lot, I mean it's actually a lot of food. Like, objectively. It's not just me feeling like I ate a normal meal and getting upset about it. It's... it's a huge amount. I don't think I ever feel that way about just a regular portion.
After these late-night eating episodes, do you often feel guilty, ashamed, or depressed about what you've done?

Yeah, absolutely. I feel terrible afterward. It's... it's a lot of guilt. I just sit there looking at all the empty wrappers and feel really ashamed of myself. It definitely brings my mood down, just feeling like I have no control over it.
Do these late-night eating episodes usually happen after a particularly stressful day, or do they sometimes occur even when your day was relatively calm?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't noticed a specific pattern with that. It seems like they can happen whether it was a stressful day or just a regular, calm one. It's usually just tied to getting home late after my shift, no matter how the actual day went at work.
